alignments.note: Chain rendered attributively; the single supplied determiner is the construct noun's (rules 28, 29), discontinuous around the attributive (rule 25).
Supplied indefinite article with the construct noun (rules 15, 29).

Anarthrous participle takes the supplied *he that* that makes it a noun phrase (rule 46) and the construction-supplied copula (rule 20), headed on the word carrying the lexeme. The competing reading takes the fronted nominal as the Hebrew predicate and puts *Is* there instead (rules 8, 20).
Adverbial accusative takes the supplied preposition (rule 33); chain rendered attributively, so the supplied determiner is the construct noun's (rule 29).

review_notes: The copula is placed on the participial predicate, which is also where the English clause puts it; the note on that unit records the competing reading.
